starting_wwox_observation: Neuron-targeted deletion at P17: fewer CC1-positive and more PDGFRa-positive callosal cells and fewer myelinated axons (INV06:E08, E09; 3 v 3 mice, a measurement limit); co-culture: fewer myelinating-class cells on null DRG, in a B27/N2 medium with no named hormone (INV06:E06, C01); spheroids: hormone added to the differentiation medium and withdrawn from Day 71 (INV06:E12)
external_relation_used: A differently-caused hypomyelination (thyroid-hormone transport deficit) shows the same stage pattern (PMID37307933 abstract, see comparison ALT3), fewer parvalbumin interneurons (N03), callosal myelin staining normalised by a receptor agonist only when started in the first three postnatal weeks (N01, N02), a T3 rescue lost in older zebrafish larvae while the analogues (TRIAC, DITPA) still rescued oligodendrocyte number there (N14, corrected after the audit; this conflicts with the mouse late-start result N02, so a 'closing window' for an analogue lever is not shown) and receptor-beta ligand effects on OPCs in vitro (N06). This is a transfer
action_required: Two conditional arms, neither presented as favourable. Arm A (block is receptor-responsive): more thyroid-receptor activation in OPCs on null neurons releases maturation, with a larger effect than on wild-type neurons. Arm B (block not receptor-limited): activation acts equally on both genotypes or not at all, and the WWOX-specific reading is closed
target_or_process: Thyroid-hormone-receptor-dependent OPC differentiation (THRA, THRB) and the hormone content of the culture medium, as a process; not hormone supplementation
compound_or_probe_if_sustainable: Tiratricol (CAT:CHEMBL41632) with liothyronine (CAT:CHEMBL1544) as comparator, as in INV-12; sobetirome (CAT:CHEMBL107400) only as a receptor-beta-leaning isoform control; DITPA (CAT:CHEMBL2348292) as a second analogue. TG68 and IS25 are absent from the catalogue (no identifier assigned) and TG68 has stated off-receptor activity (N07): not proposed
identity_and_pharmacology: Source facts: tiratricol and DITPA activate thyroid receptors without MCT8-dependent entry (introduction of PMID36834863); sobetirome is the best-known receptor-beta-selective analogue and IS25 a receptor-beta agonist (EC50 448 nM in the source) (PMID37765015). Caveats from sources: the exposure that normalised brain readouts suppressed the mouse thyroid axis (N04); the human trial of tiratricol had no neurodevelopmental endpoint (N05); sobetirome stopped at phase 1 and eprotirome terminated (N11); seizure effect mixed per INV-12 (not re-read). No dose, no regimen; a hormone is a lever of a process here, not a proposal to give it
hypothesised_benefit: If Arm A: partial release of the OPC-to-mature step in the dish and a reason to ask a pre-onset in vivo question (INV-12). No claim on conduction, development or quality of life
main_counterevidence: No WWOX material shows a thyroid-hormone deficit; the one WWOX-thyroid hit was an unrelated human GWAS (N20). The stage pattern is generic (also with creatine deficiency, comparison ALT3). Late start did not help in the model (N02) and nulls die at 3 to 4 weeks, leaving a narrow window. Trials show no neurological improvement as a recurrent observation (N15). T3 did not rescue a cytokine block in vitro (N08). Isoform dispute (N09)
context_where_useless_or_harmful: If the deficit is carried by an absent cue or by activity (INV06 H1, H2): an agonist acts downstream and may raise counts without function, as neonatal clemastine did (INV06:E39); after the early window (N02; N14 conflicts for analogues); in seizure-prone tissue (INV-12, mixed); in an inflammatory block where the natural ligand fails (N08)
result_that_would_weaken_it: Agonist raises maturation equally on wild-type and null neurons; or no change once the medium hormone baseline is defined and target engagement shown; or rescue only in the spheroid (hormone withdrawn) and not in the DRG co-culture or S-KO tissue (medium confound); or hormone-target transcripts not lower in null OPCs or brain
wwox_evidence_vs_transfer: WWOX: stage pattern (INV06:E08), co-culture deficit (INV06:E06), medium composition (C01, INV06:E12). Transfer: all thyroid-deprivation, rescue-window and ligand evidence (N01 to N15). The overlap of stage pattern and parvalbumin loss with a hormone-deprived brain is an INFERENZA, not a cause
depth_of_sources: PMID36834863 and PMID37765015 partial full text (text read, figures not viewed); PMID27664134, PMID32477268, PMID37307933 abstract only; held PMID33914858 Methods only

starting_wwox_observation: Wwox-null mice are hypoglycaemic from the second week and neuronal restoration normalises glucose together with myelin, bundled (C07, C08); no glucose result for the neuron-targeted line in the held text (C03); the co-culture deficit appears in a defined medium where systemic hypoglycaemia cannot act (INV06:E05, E06); lactate is higher in Wwox-loss human fibroblasts (4 of 4 conditions) and a glycolysis/lactate transcript module is higher in sign inside its null in P47T knock-in hippocampus (NEED-PDH-PYRUVATE-AXIS O1, O5): opposite in sign to a supply deficit
external_relation_used: Low glucose lowers oligodendrocyte-lineage cell number and myelination in cultured cortical slices, rescued by lactate; white-matter oligodendrocytes take up lactate by MCT1 (N12, N13, abstract only); Glut1 haploinsufficiency lowers brain glucose, glycogen and lactate with striatal myelin-gene downregulation and a lactate rescue of motor deficits (other readouts are not stated in the abstract; the abstract also reports myelin-lipid reductions, region not stated) (C10 to C12). Transfer from energy-deprivation systems
action_required: Two conditional arms. Arm A (energy-limited lineage): availability of lactate or glucose to the oligodendrocyte lineage on null neurons must rise. Arm B (flux reversed or mis-signalled): null neurons release more lactate or run a glycolytic shift, so the needed action would be lower glycolytic output; Arm B has no myelin-specific source and rests on the fibroblast datum alone (IPOTESI)
target_or_process: Glucose and lactate availability to the oligodendrocyte lineage (GLUT1 SLC2A1, MCT1 SLC16A1 uptake) and neuronal glycolytic output, as a process
compound_or_probe_if_sustainable: No compound sustained. Lactate is a metabolite probe in the sources (catalogue CAT:EC:01903, no status statement), used to test a process, not a supplementation proposal. No MCT1 blocker is named in any source read (the Rinholm full text was not reachable), so none is proposed
identity_and_pharmacology: Source facts only: white-matter oligodendrocytes take up L-lactate through MCT1 (N13); early-postnatal lactate partly rescued motor deficits in a Glut1-deficient mouse (C12), a symptom response and not myelin protection. Caveat: a metabolic intervention in a child with seizures has developmental and acid-base effects not examined here. No dose
hypothesised_benefit: If Arm A: the dish deficit shrinks with matched energy supply, placing part of the cause in supply rather than cue or activity. No inference to function
main_counterevidence: Lactate rescue in Glut1 deficiency was motor, not shown for myelin (C12); myelin and MRI findings there were striatal (C10, C11); the Rinholm result is cortical slices under low glucose at abstract level; WWOX-side lactate points up not down; no brain energy measurement in a Wwox-null mouse was found in the two held texts searched for lactate (C09); a fly neuronal wwox knockdown paper reporting raised lactate (PMID 42909904, abstract only, found by the auditor) points the same way as the WWOX-side lactate data; hypoglycaemia starts in week 2 and the myelin readout is P17, so order is unset (C07); the bundled rescue cannot separate glucose from seizures (C08)
context_where_useless_or_harmful: If the deficit does not change with energy arms; in tissue with sufficient supply; in Arm B contexts where extra lactate adds to an existing overflow; acid load in the dish is unassessed
result_that_would_weaken_it: Null and wild-type neurons show the same glucose consumption, lactate release and respiration in the co-culture medium and energy arms leave the deficit unchanged; or fixed null neurons (no metabolism) reproduce the deficit, which places it in the substrate
wwox_evidence_vs_transfer: WWOX: hypoglycaemia and bundled rescue (C07, C08), module lactate rows (non-neural cells, transcripts). Transfer: all oligodendrocyte-energy evidence (N12, N13, C10 to C12)
depth_of_sources: PMID21228163 and PMID42686079 abstract only; held PMID34747138 and PMID33914858 partial (keyword searches and Results passages)
